statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit across seven representative paths. Not covered: authenticated library, completed payment, account cancellation and mature-content gates because they require credentials or a financial commitment.

page.framework: server-rendered MPA with jQuery/Slick-era shared chrome
page.notes: Public Japanese comic catalog/store. The homepage, listing, search, detail, guest reader, account entry and recovery archetypes were sampled. Authenticated and paid states were excluded to avoid account/financial actions.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is byte-identical in appearance to the light capture; the probe reports color-scheme: normal and white surfaces.
Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the probe found zero active animations and zero computed animation/transition durations.
The prefers-contrast probe found no contrast/forced-colors rules; Lighthouse measured free-chapter labels at 3.73:1, below 4.5:1.
The homepage-to-free video contains only discrete before/after frames; page inspection found no authored view-transition CSS despite multipage navigation.
No parallax, scrollytelling, or scroll-linked reveal effect was present on the representative surfaces.
checkOutcomes.reason: The site does not use scroll-linked motion, so there is no scroll-handler implementation to assess.

checkOutcomes.evidence: DOM/CSS capture identifies .slick-slider, translated tracks and scripted arrows; no scroll-snap implementation was observed.
The homepage is about 10,897px tall, while CSS/DOM evidence shows static 173px header chrome and no scroll-state query/progress affordance.
No tooltip, popup menu or edge-positioned transient overlay was present on the exercised guest surfaces.
checkOutcomes.reason: There was no anchored overlay whose attachment or fallback placement could be judged.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Breadcrumbs on listing/detail/search pages, descriptive section headings, and the book-to-reader action consistently identify location and next step.
No load-time modal, consent wall, or full-viewport interruption obscured content across the representative pages.
No guest-path modal or transient overlay was encountered; DOM probe reported zero dialog, popover and details elements.
checkOutcomes.reason: No dismissible overlay was present in the tested guest journey.

checkOutcomes.method: Desktop screenshot and page layout review
checkOutcomes.evidence: The desktop page devotes the main canvas to catalog content, covers, rankings and reading actions; shared chrome is compact relative to the long content page.
Layout measured scrollWidth 768 versus clientWidth 360, a 408px overflow, on both home and book detail; every mobile screenshot except the special 404 clips key content and controls.
The probe found zero container rules; shared header/nav and content components remain desktop-sized and clipped on all five mobile archetypes.
Focus/target probe measured the search input and button at 24px high and account links at 11px high; nav targets are 39px high. Keyboard outlines are visible, but touch sizing is insufficient.
The logo, search box, free-comics navigation, catalog sections, detailed title and “今すぐ無料で読む” action clearly communicate purpose and next steps.

checkOutcomes.method: Guest journey walkthrough plus mobile account screenshots
checkOutcomes.evidence: The guest search → book detail → free chapter journey completes, but account registration and login controls are clipped off-screen at 360px.
An unknown URL returns a clear Japanese error message, search, a large “トップページへ” recovery action and useful destination links.
Lighthouse performance scored 0.39 with LCP 7.9s, TBT 510ms and CLS 0.146; the first-party trace corroborated 2.44s LCP under a lighter desktop run.
Lighthouse measured CLS 0.146 and three shifts; the image audit found all 100 inspected images lacked width and height attributes.
Lighthouse reported 4.3s main-thread work, 2.5s script boot time and 510ms TBT; HAR recorded 78 script requests.
HAR recorded 388 requests and 11,694,781 transferred bytes; Lighthouse estimated 1.92s render-blocking savings, 1.12MB cache-lifetime savings and 650ms document-latency savings.
Lighthouse estimated 1,974KiB removable unused JavaScript plus 74KiB legacy-JS savings; 78 script requests transferred 3.29MB.
DOM probes show the search input has no associated label or aria-label, and multiple chapter checkboxes have empty label text.
Lighthouse’s axe audit repeatedly measured #cf6363 text on white at 3.73:1 for 13px bold free-chapter labels, below 4.5:1.
Semantic probe found one H1 with empty text; focus is visible but only as a 1px auto outline, while heading hierarchy starts with promotional H2 sections.
At 360px, catalog headings, product details, payment explanations and login choices extend hundreds of pixels beyond the viewport.
Lighthouse failed meta-viewport because user-scalable=no or maximum-scale<5; independent layout evidence measured 408px overflow at 360px.
Lighthouse failed errors-in-console; the retained Lighthouse JSON contains the affected console records.
Image audit found 100/100 images without dimensions, 43 oversized, 87 below-fold images not lazy-loaded, 37 without srcset and 65 in legacy formats.
Lighthouse reported one deprecated-API warning, Inspector Issues, and three reasons preventing back/forward cache restoration.
Homepage and book detail expose unique descriptive titles and meta descriptions in raw server HTML.
Robots/sitemap and real hrefs are present, yet mobile layouts overflow by 408px and the link probe lists numerous empty-text hero anchors.
Both audited public templates return 200, expose canonical URLs, remain indexable, and robots.txt references a populated sitemap.
Book detail includes matching Product, AggregateRating and BreadcrumbList JSON-LD plus complete Open Graph title, description, URL, type and image.
Headers show HSTS/nosniff/XFO but no CSP; cookie audit found four non-Secure cookies and several SameSite=None cookies. Secret scan found no exposed credentials.
Tracker capture found 14 third-party origins and five known tracker families including Facebook, Google Analytics and DoubleClick; HAR shows extensive network activity.

checkOutcomes.method: Initial load and login screenshot/DOM review
checkOutcomes.evidence: No permission prompt appeared on load, and login offers established federated identity providers rather than presenting a password-only form on the tested surface.
HSTS, X-Frame-Options, nosniff and Referrer-Policy are present, but CSP and Permissions-Policy are missing.
The book detail retains 93% rendered-content coverage without JavaScript and keeps title, H1 and description; homepage is not an empty shell and retains key metadata/navigation.
Guest search, product selection and free reading complete; the dedicated 404 state is coherent and actionable.
Platform probe found no manifest link and zero service-worker registrations on the interactive reading/catalog experience.
The representative HTTP failure state explains the problem and offers search, home and catalog recovery routes rather than a blank shell.

checkOutcomes.method: Site intent inferred from rendered content and Service metadata
checkOutcomes.evidence: JSON-LD declares areaServed Japan and all audited commerce/content surfaces are deliberately Japanese-only; no locale-sensitive date, currency conversion or event scheduling flow was present.
checkOutcomes.reason: This run found a single-language, Japan-only service and no user-facing locale/time-zone data to test.

checkOutcomes.method: Homepage, detail, reader and registration visual review
checkOutcomes.evidence: No consent wall, confirmshaming, disguised advertisement control or forced-continuity prompt interrupted the guest flow; free and paid states are visibly labelled.

The exercised guest search and registration-choice surfaces did not expose a user-entered validation form; the available controls are links/search and no invalid state could be meaningfully triggered.
checkOutcomes.reason: No representative required-field form was available before authentication in the tested scope.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Authentication is provider/link based and the only public text input is search, where browser autocomplete remains enabled by default.
At 360px, registration payment tiles, explanatory terms and login-provider choices extend off the visible canvas.
HAR transferred 7.58MB of images; image audit found 43 oversized images, 65 legacy-format images, 37 missing responsive sources and Lighthouse estimated 5.13MB image savings.
A guest homepage load made 388 requests, including 78 scripts and 45 XHR/fetches, while Lighthouse measured 4.3s main-thread work.
Fourteen third-party origins load alongside a 10–11.7MB page; 228 image requests dominate at 7.58MB and many below-fold images load eagerly.
Platform probe found no WebMCP registration, although product metadata and purchase/read actions make this a plausible agentic-commerce surface.
No summarisation, translation or other inference feature is offered on the audited surfaces, so there is no server inference decision to replace.
checkOutcomes.reason: The current product does not expose an inference-dependent user feature.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Across 20 repeated carousel advances, live DOM count stabilised at 2,859 and heap rose between collections then dropped from 66.7MB to 54.3MB at GC, rather than growing monotonically.

checkOutcomes.method: Heap primitive totals and runtime metrics
checkOutcomes.evidence: Heap snapshots reported about 29–47MB self size for a media-heavy catalog; runtime heap was collected and remained recoverable under repeated interaction.
The live DOM count changed only from 2,855 to 2,859 across 20 carousel advances and then remained flat; no accumulating animation objects were observed.

principleOutcomes.reason: All checks were judged not applicable for this site.

paths.description: Homepage and global navigation: primary discovery surface and shared site chrome.
Search for キングダム: representative search/results journey.
Book 245447: representative product/detail page with structured metadata and free chapters.
First free chapter from book 245447: guest core reading flow.
Registration and login surfaces: representative account/commercial flow.
Unknown URL: representative HTTP error/recovery state.

findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark-theme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is byte-identical in appearance to the light capture; the probe reports color-scheme: normal and white surfaces.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and supply preference-driven surface/text tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Contrast preferences are not supported and some essential labels are already below WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: The prefers-contrast probe found no contrast/forced-colors rules; Lighthouse measured free-chapter labels at 3.73:1, below 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Use system colors or forced-color-adjust-aware styling under forced-colors and strengthen low-contrast text tokens.

findings.summary: Route changes are abrupt rather than continuity-preserving.
findings.evidence: The homepage-to-free video contains only discrete before/after frames; page inspection found no authored view-transition CSS despite multipage navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Enable same-origin cross-document View Transitions with @view-transition and provide reduced-motion-safe fallbacks.

findings.summary: The hero carousel uses legacy scripted Slick behavior instead of native scroll-snap semantics.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS capture identifies .slick-slider, translated tracks and scripted arrows; no scroll-snap implementation was observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the carousel as an overflow scroller with scroll-snap, native touch behavior and accessible controls; layer decoration on top.

findings.summary: Long catalog pages do not provide scroll-state-aware navigation or progress context.
findings.evidence: The homepage is about 10,897px tall, while CSS/DOM evidence shows static 173px header chrome and no scroll-state query/progress affordance.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact sticky header that responds to scroll state and consider a progress or return-to-top affordance on very long pages.

findings.summary: Primary pages render a 768px desktop canvas inside a 360px viewport.
findings.evidence: Layout measured scrollWidth 768 versus clientWidth 360, a 408px overflow, on both home and book detail; every mobile screenshot except the special 404 clips key content and controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the fixed 768px canvas with intrinsic/fluid layout, wrap navigation, constrain media to max-inline-size:100%, and verify all templates at 320–400px.

findings.summary: Reused catalog, header and account components do not adapt within narrow containers.
findings.evidence: The probe found zero container rules; shared header/nav and content components remain desktop-sized and clipped on all five mobile archetypes.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable components containment and use size container queries to switch layout, typography and action placement based on available inline size.

findings.summary: Several primary controls are far below recommended touch-target size.
findings.evidence: Focus/target probe measured the search input and button at 24px high and account links at 11px high; nav targets are 39px high. Keyboard outlines are visible, but touch sizing is insufficient.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase interactive hit areas to at least 44px where practical while retaining visible :focus-visible outlines and non-hover labels.

findings.summary: Mobile load performance misses the Core Web Vitals quality bar.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse performance scored 0.39 with LCP 7.9s, TBT 510ms and CLS 0.146; the first-party trace corroborated 2.44s LCP under a lighter desktop run.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP asset, reduce server/document latency, defer non-critical scripts and monitor field LCP/INP/CLS.

findings.summary: Unsized images create avoidable layout-shift risk.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured CLS 0.146 and three shifts; the image audit found all 100 inspected images lacked width and height attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image space with width/height or aspect-ratio and use stable font fallbacks.

findings.summary: Heavy JavaScript blocks the main thread during mobile load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported 4.3s main-thread work, 2.5s script boot time and 510ms TBT; HAR recorded 78 script requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile heavy scripts, remove unneeded tag/feature code, split long work and schedule non-urgent tasks by priority.

findings.summary: The critical network path is large and inefficient.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 388 requests and 11,694,781 transferred bytes; Lighthouse estimated 1.92s render-blocking savings, 1.12MB cache-lifetime savings and 650ms document-latency savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Shorten render-blocking chains, set effective immutable caching for versioned assets, preload only the LCP resource and improve document delivery.

findings.summary: The homepage ships substantial unused and legacy JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 1,974KiB removable unused JavaScript plus 74KiB legacy-JS savings; 78 script requests transferred 3.29MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Use coverage to remove unused bundles, conditionally load optional features and reduce duplicated third-party tags.

findings.summary: The shared search input and chapter-selection controls lack robust labels.
findings.evidence: DOM probes show the search input has no associated label or aria-label, and multiple chapter checkboxes have empty label text.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide persistent visible labels or programmatic names for search and each chapter checkbox; keep native roles.

findings.summary: Free-chapter action text fails minimum contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse’s axe audit repeatedly measured #cf6363 text on white at 3.73:1 for 13px bold free-chapter labels, below 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken the action-text token or adjust its background until normal text reaches at least 4.5:1 in every state.

findings.summary: The homepage has an empty H1 and relies on minimal browser-default focus treatment.
findings.evidence: Semantic probe found one H1 with empty text; focus is visible but only as a 1px auto outline, while heading hierarchy starts with promotional H2 sections.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the homepage one descriptive H1 and strengthen consistent :focus-visible treatment without changing logical tab order.

findings.summary: Mobile clipping breaks reading order and hides text and controls.
findings.evidence: At 360px, catalog headings, product details, payment explanations and login choices extend hundreds of pixels beyond the viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Reflow content to one column at narrow sizes, allow text to wrap, and avoid fixed inline dimensions.

findings.summary: The viewport restricts zoom and the page does not reflow.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed meta-viewport because user-scalable=no or maximum-scale<5; independent layout evidence measured 408px overflow at 360px.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove user-scalable=no/low maximum-scale, preserve pinch zoom and make all templates reflow at 320 CSS pixels.

findings.summary: The page logs browser errors during load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed errors-in-console; the retained Lighthouse JSON contains the affected console records.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix first-party exceptions and failed resources, and gate noisy third-party failures so production loads cleanly.

findings.summary: Image delivery and sizing are systematically unsound.
findings.evidence: Image audit found 100/100 images without dimensions, 43 oversized, 87 below-fold images not lazy-loaded, 37 without srcset and 65 in legacy formats.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic dimensions, responsive srcset/sizes, lazy-load below-fold images and use AVIF/WebP where suitable.

findings.summary: The page triggers deprecation, DevTools Issues and BFCache failures.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported one deprecated-API warning, Inspector Issues, and three reasons preventing back/forward cache restoration.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated APIs, resolve DevTools Issues and lifecycle/BFCache blockers, and ensure modern source maps are available.

findings.summary: Content is crawlable, but the public pages are not mobile-friendly and many promotional anchors have no text node.
findings.evidence: Robots/sitemap and real hrefs are present, yet mobile layouts overflow by 408px and the link probe lists numerous empty-text hero anchors.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep real hrefs and image alternatives, add descriptive textual link names, and make public templates reflow on mobile.

findings.summary: HTTPS is present, but CSP is absent and multiple cookies use weak transport/cross-site settings.
findings.evidence: Headers show HSTS/nosniff/XFO but no CSP; cookie audit found four non-Secure cookies and several SameSite=None cookies. Secret scan found no exposed credentials.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP and mark HTTPS-only cookies Secure with the narrowest workable SameSite and HttpOnly settings.

findings.summary: A large tracking footprint loads before the user takes an action.
findings.evidence: Tracker capture found 14 third-party origins and five known tracker families including Facebook, Google Analytics and DoubleClick; HAR shows extensive network activity.
findings.suggestedFix: Inventory each third party, remove nonessential trackers, delay consent-dependent code and batch/minimise analytics events.

findings.summary: Defensive browser policy coverage is incomplete.
findings.evidence: HSTS, X-Frame-Options, nosniff and Referrer-Policy are present, but CSP and Permissions-Policy are missing.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrictive CSP including frame-ancestors and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy; evaluate Trusted Types for script-sensitive surfaces.

findings.summary: The app-like comic store has no installed web app manifest or service worker fallback.
findings.evidence: Platform probe found no manifest link and zero service-worker registrations on the interactive reading/catalog experience.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a manifest and a narrowly scoped service worker that serves an offline shell/fallback while never caching sensitive purchase responses.

findings.summary: Account and payment-choice screens are not safely reviewable on a phone because commitments and controls are clipped.
findings.evidence: At 360px, registration payment tiles, explanatory terms and login-provider choices extend off the visible canvas.
findings.suggestedFix: Reflow commercial/account screens so pricing, terms, provider identity and reversal/navigation actions are fully visible before commitment.

findings.summary: Image payload is far larger than needed for displayed sizes.
findings.evidence: HAR transferred 7.58MB of images; image audit found 43 oversized images, 65 legacy-format images, 37 missing responsive sources and Lighthouse estimated 5.13MB image savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate correctly sized AVIF/WebP variants, provide srcset/sizes and avoid downloading hidden carousel clones.

findings.summary: The initial page performs disproportionate background/network work.
findings.evidence: A guest homepage load made 388 requests, including 78 scripts and 45 XHR/fetches, while Lighthouse measured 4.3s main-thread work.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer nonessential fetches until intent/visibility, consolidate analytics and remove work for off-screen or duplicated carousel content.

findings.summary: Third-party and promotional media cost is disproportionate to first-viewport value.
findings.evidence: Fourteen third-party origins load alongside a 10–11.7MB page; 228 image requests dominate at 7.58MB and many below-fold images load eagerly.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party/media budget, lazy-load below-fold catalog imagery and only activate optional trackers after justified consent or interaction.

findings.summary: The commerce/catalog experience exposes no structured agent capability surface.
findings.evidence: Platform probe found no WebMCP registration, although product metadata and purchase/read actions make this a plausible agentic-commerce surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose narrowly scoped read/search/catalog tools first, with confirmation and policy boundaries around account or purchase actions.
